title: Set `ImageDataSettings` to have `colorSpace` default to `"srgb"`
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Background:
* this was added to the spec in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/6562
* in that CL, I was unsure of the choice (see the request for feedback [here](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/6562#issuecomment-822798470))
* this came up again in the TAG review, where the shipped behavior [was decided on](https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/646#issuecomment-859135275) (search for "Am I reading it correctly that getImageData() will return sRGB data even in a P3 canvas").
* there is a reference to a WhatWG review that came to the opposite conclusion, but I can't find any documentation of it

Having lived with that choice for a while, I don't think it was right one to make.

First reason is just the complexity of the spec. The [algorithm to initialize an `ImageData`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#initialize-an-imagedata-object) has a separate parameter for the color space which is set to `"srgb"` sometimes and in other times set to a property of the caller.

Second reason is that it is probably worse for naive callers to get this behavior. The one case where this is good is if some is just doing a getImageData-then-putImageData. I suspect that that case is rare. It's more likely that a naive caller is going to expect sRGB pixels. There are very few pixel manipulation algorithms that are independent of color space.

Third reason is that it's a messy precedent. As we add things like premultiplied alpha (https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/5371), this starts to get messy. Then for pixel format support (https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10856), inferring a default from `CanvasRenderingContext2D` is not guaranteed to always have a natural mapping (for now the two are in lock-step, but this is not guaranteed to remain the case).

So in this issue I'd like to 
1. Resolve that we should not add any more optional parameters to `ImageDataSettings`. All future parameters should be specified.
2. Determine if it's possible to un-do this behavior in the case of `colorSpace`. It has been shipping for 3 years. What sort of usage statistics would be needed to determine if we can break compatibility this way?
